content:
Samir: sharing results from yesterday's perf run + a sketch for an adaptive eviction watermark. ran into p95 spikes when prefill dominates kv cache and workspace allocs
Priya: nice, plz drop the profiler snippets
Samir: paste below — short summary: workload is mix of short chat and long-context summaries. when sequence_length > 2k we see massive workspace churn and slab fragmentation. p50 stable, p95 jumps ~3-4x when kv-prefill ratio > 0.6
Samir: profiler snippet:
```
cmd: ./perf-run --model redwood-xl-8k --batch 8 --trace
GPU0 total=40GB used=36.1GB free=3.9GB
KV cache occupancy: 68% (active 52% prefills 16%)
Slab fragmentation: 17.8% (hot: 24MB, cold: 1.2GB)
Alloc failures: 12 (OOM soft-reserve triggered)
latency p50=48ms p95=320ms p99=840ms
```
Jordan: hmm that fragmentation number is higher than usual. do we know whether it's prefill objects or decode tmp buffers?
Samir: looks mixed. prefill allocations dominate the mid-size slabs (8-64KB), decode creates many transient ~4-16KB buffers. when both spike we end up with holes that block larger workspace requests.
Alex: did you try lowering prefills per-request or adding per-request soft caps? we had a small rollback on that for canary last month but didn't have telemetry like this
Samir: yes. ran two experiments: A) per-request prefill cap=2MB B) adaptive watermark eviction (sketch below). results: A reduced p95 by ~18% but increased model token cost by ~6% (more decode re-prefetch). B reduced p95 by ~33% and reduced peak mem slightly; fragmentation reduced to ~11%
Priya: adaptive watermark? describe the policy
Samir: policy idea — maintain two watermarks: soft_wm and hard_wm. soft_wm = target usable mem threshold (eg 75% of GPU), hard_wm = emergency threshold (eg 90%). allow prefill and decode to allocate normally under soft_wm. once usage crosses soft_wm, start evicting least-recent-prefill segments with an eviction score that weights age, size, reuse_probability. below hard_wm we prefer evicting entire large contiguous prefill slots to free workspace for kernel buffers. if above hard_wm, start throttle/deprioritize prefill and reject large continuous prefetches. also coalesce small free chunks into a recycle list for future decode temps.
Jordan: sounds good. how do kernels interact? like if kernel selection picks a memory-hungry algorithm we need to reserve headroom
Samir: exactly. we feed kernel_selection a headroom hint: desired_workspace_reserve = max( model_workspace_estimate * kernel_memory_multiplier, fixed_minimum ) and the allocator ensures that free_contiguous >= desired_workspace_reserve or triggers eviction policy before kernel switches to that kernel. if kernel can't get contiguous memory, it falls back to a lower-memory kernel path (slower but stable).
Alex: any pseudo-code or config we can rollout behind a flag?
Samir: quick sketch:
```
// on alloc request R
if free_total < soft_wm_threshold:
  run_eviction(eviction_budget = min( soft_wm_threshold - free_total + R.size, max_eviction_budget ))
if free_contiguous < R.contig_need:
  try_coalesce_small_free()
  if free_contiguous < R.contig_need:
    if current_usage < hard_wm_threshold:
      evict_large_contiguous_slots()
    else:
      if R.type == PREFILL:
        throttle_or_reject_prefill(R)
      else:
        fallback_to_low_mem_kernel(R)
```
Priya: that looks safe. question: eviction score math? we want to avoid thrashing by evicting something that will immediately be refilled
Samir: score = alpha * age_seconds + beta * (1 - reuse_prob) + gamma * size_penalty + delta * fragmentation_impact. reuse_prob from recent access hist. tune alpha>>beta to bias towards oldest items.
Jordan: how did you compute reuse_prob? sliding window of accesses per key?
Samir: yes, 5m window, decay factor, maintain tiny per-key counters (we already have this telemetry in V2). cheap approximation: hits_last_5m / (hits_last_5m + misses_last_5m)
Alex: results you mentioned — numbers are from single-node bench or canary?
Samir: single-node synthetic harness with mixed seq distribution + production-ish trace replay. canary will run tomorrow. details: B (watermark) run stats:
```
prefill rate -30% (because we throttled some prefetches)
p95 latency -33%
fragmentation 17.8% -> 11.2%
alloc failures 12 -> 2
token cost +1.2% (mostly from re-decode overhead)
```
Priya: token cost small — acceptable tradeoff for stability. any regression risk on tail for tiny requests?
Samir: minor increase in p50 for tiny chat due to slightly more conservative kernel selection (~+6ms). but overall p95 improvement is worth it.
Jordan: what about per-request cap tuning? maybe combine both: small cap for background prefetch and adaptive for heavy requests
Samir: agreed. my plan: rollout B behind feature-flag + conservative defaults (soft_wm 72%, hard_wm 88%), enable detailed telemetry: per-alloc type hist, eviction decisions, kernel fallback rate. run week-long canary and check p95, alloc failures, token delta
Alex: can you add a dashboard panel for 'eviction_effectiveness' that shows reclaimed bytes vs re-prefetched bytes over time? also show kernel_fallback_rate
Samir: will add. I'll push a PR for allocator + kernel hint API. CI note: added unit tests for coalescing, plus a microbench that simulates 10k reqs with mixed sizes
ci-bot: build passed for branch samir/watermark-evict (linux-gpu, integration) :white_check_mark:
Priya: great. please tag me on the PR. also include a short runbook: when to disable (if token delta > 5% or kernel_fallback_rate > 8%)
Samir: will do. next: planning to test different eviction_score weights to find knee point where re-prefetch cost outweighs fragmentation benefit
Alex: ping me when canary results are in, I want to compare against last month's per-request cap rollback stats
Samir: will update thread after canary (scheduled 2618080000). thanks all :thumbsup:
